en: Born **15 October 1885** at **Efri-Ey** in **Meðalland**, south Iceland — **9th of 13 kids** (his parents clearly had stamina). ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Jóhannes Sveinsson Kjarval
en: Crew saw his sketches, **passed the hat**, the fishermen's union topped it up. **1911**: **London's Royal Academy slammed the door.** The rejection was the redirect — **1912** to **Copenhagen** and the **Royal Danish Academy** (graduated **1917**).

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Jóhannes Sveinsson Kjarval
en: Home again he painted Iceland knelt over the **moss and lava three inches from his nose**, swearing he saw **elves and hidden folk** in the cracks. (In Iceland, that's not a diagnosis — that's a career.)

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Jóhannes Sveinsson Kjarval
en: **1914**: his **Bakkagerði** altarpiece shows Christ preaching from **Álfaborg**, the elf-rock, **Dyrfjöll** behind. A second altarpiece, dismissed as "crude and ugly," was bought by **Halldór Laxness** for **Gljúfrasteinn** (we pass it later). One man, two altarpieces, **zero bishops convinced.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Jóhannes Sveinsson Kjarval
en: He painted roughly **5,000 works — and gave most away**, dying **owning almost nothing.** That grey block in Klambratún is **Kjarvalsstaðir**, Iceland's **first purpose-built art museum** (1973); since **1995** his face is on the **2,000-króna note** — the only cod fisherman ever **promoted to legal tender.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölgerðin Egill Skallagrímsson
en: Two years later Iceland bans **all alcohol** (1915) — so Tómas sails to **Copenhagen and Germany (1915–17) to learn brewing anyway**, training up for a product his own country just outlawed. Wine creeps back in **1922**, spirits in **1935**, but **beer stays illegal until 1989** — because it read as **Danish**, and sipping a Danish lager while fighting Denmark for independence felt like treason.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Elliðaárdalur & Paradísardalur
en: A volcano split the river. The Vikings claimed it. The British fortified it. The river is still working overtime to undo all of it.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Elliðaárdalur & Paradísardalur
en: The whole valley was redesigned **~5,000 years ago** when **Leiti** erupted: lava poured down, hit the river and **split it in two**. Before, one river; after, two. Every waterfall here is the river's **5,000-year project** to saw back through solid basalt to the sea.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Elliðaárdalur & Paradísardalur
en: The Elliðaá is one of the only **capital-city rivers on Earth with a wild Atlantic salmon run** — around **1,500–2,500** shove upstream past the joggers each summer. Reykjavík was so smitten it **bought the whole river in 1906.** (Your city buys parks. We bought a river.)

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Elliðaárdalur & Paradísardalur
en: One kilometre of valley has hosted a **1750s wool mill**, a **drowning pool at Skötufoss** for women convicted of "moral crimes," outlaws in the lava tubes, **British WWII Quonset huts**, and a century-old hydro plant — **Elliðaárstöð (1921)**, still humming.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Elliðaárdalur & Paradísardalur
en: Most Icelandically of all: a **1998 burst pipe** flooded the valley and, in a single weekend, **washed 10,000 years of buried history back into daylight.** Even the plumbing does archaeology here.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Hellisheiðarvirkjun
en: We're on the **Hengill volcanic system**, a rare **plate-boundary triple junction on dry land**. Water goes down, returns at nearly **300°C**, and spins turbines — the white plumes are **steam**, not smoke. Built up in stages **2006–2011** to **303 MW**, it's **Iceland's largest geothermal power station**.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Hellisheiðarvirkjun
en: After the electricity, the leftover hot water runs **27 km** in insulated pipes to heat **more than half the capital region** — nothing wasted, and Reykjavík never has to reach for a jumper.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Hellisheiðarvirkjun
en: Via **CarbFix**, CO₂ is dissolved in water and pumped into hot basalt, where **~95% turns to solid rock within about two years** (Matter et al., 2016). Next door, **Climeworks' "Mammoth"** plant (2024) sucks CO₂ straight from the air — up to **36,000 tonnes a year** — for the same rock treatment.

ctx: the point of the block — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: Every drop that fell on the Golden Circle — glaciers, geysers, lakes — eventually squeezes through this one 25 km channel.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: The Golden Circle gets the postcards. This river is where the whole day quietly ends.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: Only **~25 km long**, yet **Iceland's largest river by discharge** — about **423 m³ every second** off a **~5,760 km² basin**. Not the longest; just the one you absolutely could not cross.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: It's **four systems in one**. The glacial **Hvítá** runs south from **Langjökull** past **Gullfoss**, gathering **Tungufljót** and **Brúará**; the spring-fed **Sog** drains **Þingvallavatn**, Iceland's biggest natural lake. They meet just above **Selfoss** and from there run as one — the **Ölfusá**.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: It follows the **South Iceland Seismic Zone**, zig-zagging along fault lines. Beside it lies **Þjórsárhraun** — ~**8,600 years** old, ~**950 km²**, the **largest single lava flow of the whole Holocene, anywhere on Earth**.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Ölfusá
en: For centuries the **ultimate obstacle**: unfordable, no bridge, just a ferry at **Laugardælir** paid in **cattle or cod** to reach the harbour at **Eyrarbakki**. When it flooded catastrophically in **1623**, a bishop blamed a giant river serpent — an "ice worm." (It was an **ice-jam flood**; the serpent just got the better press.)

en: Hveragerði sits on a **three-way tectonic junction** on the edge of the **Hengill volcanic system** — geothermal *and* seismic, a rough combination for a postcode. Fumaroles and boiling mud pots vent **between the houses.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Hveragerði
en: On **29 May 2008** an **Mw 6.3** quake — a "doublet," two ruptures barely **2 km** out — shook the town at up to **~0.88 g** (near 1 g: the earth shoving as hard as gravity), split buildings and re-plumbed the hot springs. Rather than hide it, locals built the **Skjálftinn 2008** ("The Quake") exhibition inside the **Sunnumörk** centre, right over the fissure — stand on the crack, ride the shaking simulator.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Hveragerði
en: Cheap volcanic heat made it a **greenhouse town** from the 1920s (first geothermal greenhouse **1923**) and Iceland's **market garden**: tomatoes, cucumbers, flowers — and, at the horticultural college, **experimental bananas** planted ~**1950**: about **a tonne a year, never commercial**. Iceland is *not* a banana republic — just the most over-hyped tonne of fruit in Europe.

en: Per the saga, **Ingólfur Arnarson** threw his carved **high-seat pillars** overboard and vowed to settle wherever they washed up. Ingólfur's real title is narrower — **first *permanent* Norse settler in the saga tradition** — and he got the trophy because his family later ran the parliament and wrote the record.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Selfoss
en: The town **only exists because of the bridge.** The **1891 Ölfusárbrú** — pushed through the Alþingi by MP and banker **Tryggvi Gunnarsson** — was Iceland's **first suspension bridge**; before it the Ölfusá was uncrossable, so trade clustered at the bridgehead and **Selfoss grew up around it.** The old construction hut, **Tryggvaskáli**, is still the town's oldest building.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Selfoss
en: Then in **September 1944**, after 53 years, a milk truck tried to tow a broken-down milk truck across at the same time. The **eastern bearing cables couldn't take the concentrated weight, snapped, and dropped both trucks into the gorge.** Both drivers survived — one clung to the **truck bed until he drifted ashore** by the church.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Selfoss
en: A replacement went up in about **five and a half months**, reopening **21 December 1945** — mid-war, because the town's lifeline doesn't wait, and that span still carries you today.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Þjórsá
en: **Þjórsá** ("Bull River") rises off the **Hofsjökull** ice cap and runs **230 km** to the sea — **Iceland's longest** — draining a **7,530 km²** catchment at roughly **383 m³/s**. Not a river you paddle absent-mindedly.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Þjórsá
en: Midstream sits the island of **Árnes**, which in the settlement era hosted its own **Þing** — a local assembly. Give an Icelander a defensible rock in a fast river and the first instinct is to hold a meeting on it.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Þjórsá
en: Those wide braided channels in the fields are **floodpaths**: when the glaciers melt fast, Þjórsá spreads across its plains rather than politely staying in one channel. Its valley, **Þjórsárdalur**, is farm country that neighbour **Hekla has buried more than once** in ash.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / BSÍ Bus Terminal → Hvolsvöllur / Þjórsá
en: It does **more electrical work than any river in Iceland**: **six power stations** on the Þjórsá–Tungnaá system (Búrfell first, **1969**) feed the grid — chiefly the **aluminium smelters** that are the reason a country of 380,000 makes so much power. ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Vestmannaeyjar
en: The lucky break was weather: a storm the day before had kept the **whole fishing fleet in harbour**, so of about **5,300 residents, roughly 5,000 were evacuated in around eight hours** — Iceland has **no army**, so the fishermen ran the evacuation themselves.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Vestmannaeyjar
en: The eruption ran **five months** and buried about **400 buildings** — Iceland's own Pompeii, some houses now dug back out at the **Eldheimar museum**. To save the harbour, crews pumped **millions of litres of North Atlantic seawater** onto the advancing flow for weeks, and the cooled lava left the entrance **deeper and better sheltered than before.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Landeyjar Plains
en: The name gives it away: **Landeyjar means "land islands"** — grassy patches that stood up out of the marsh and sand. ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Landeyjar Plains
en: This "empty" plain is also **Njáls saga's stage**: **Bergþórshvoll**, where Njáll's family was burned alive around **1011**, sits out here among the hayfields. Flat, quiet — and, a thousand years ago, the address of Iceland's most famous house fire.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Markarfljót & Hlíðarendi
en: Out there: grass and sheep. In the sagas: a man who chose his view over his life — and a wife who remembered exactly how she'd been wronged.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Markarfljót & Hlíðarendi
en: In front of you the **Markarfljót** runs **~100 km** to the sea off **two ice caps sitting on live volcanoes** — **Eyjafjallajökull** and **Mýrdalsjökull** — which is why it occasionally stops being a river and becomes a **jökulhlaup**. In **2010** engineers **deliberately breached the Ring Road embankment** to let the eruption's meltwater through and **save the bridge.** Sacrifice the road to keep the crossing.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Markarfljót & Hlíðarendi
en: Tucked into the far slopes is **Hlíðarendi**, home of **Gunnar** of **Njáll's saga** — the finest fighter in Iceland, who could leap his own height in armour, backwards.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Markarfljót & Hlíðarendi
en: Sentenced to exile, Gunnar rode out, glanced back and said the line every Icelander knows: *"Fögur er hlíðin — fair is the hillside… I will not go away."* That one look cost him everything: he **turned back, stayed, and was killed** defending his farm.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Markarfljót & Hlíðarendi
en: The kicker: besieged, his bowstring cut, he asked his wife **Hallgerður** for two locks of her hair to twist a new one. She refused — payback for a slap years before — and let him die.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: A farmer here was digging ash out of his drinking water while airline CEOs were melting down 2,000 km away.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: **Eyjafjallajökull** — an **~800,000-year-old** stratovolcano, summit **1,651 m**, under an ice cap shrunk to about **66 km²** — sits there looking like a tidy white lid over green fields.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: By volcanic standards **2010 was small: a VEI 4, only ~0.27 km³ of ash.** But it fired a **plume 8–9 km high** into the **jet stream** — a small volcano in exactly the wrong spot — and the glassy particles turn jet engines into **expensive sandblasters.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: Result: the **worst aviation shutdown in Europe since WWII** — roughly **10 million travellers stranded**, airspace over some **20 countries** closed, about **100,000 flights cancelled** over six days. Europe learned volcanoes don't read timetables.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: At farms like **Þorvaldseyri** at its foot, **500–800 people were evacuated overnight** as meltwater poured off the ice; farmers **milked cows in respirator masks**, scraped ash off the roofs, then built a visitor centre — if a volcano rewrites your year you may as well sell the story.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Eyjafjallajökull
en: Guest question, every time: does it trigger **Katla** next door? The 920, 1612 and 1821 eruptions each did — but in **2010 Katla stayed shut.** A warning light, not a trigger.

en: **Rútshellir** is one of the **largest man-made caves in Iceland** — an arched hall roughly **20 m long and 2.5 m high**, hacked from the soft cliff of **Drangshlíðarfjall**, about **3 km west of Skógafoss.** Long claimed as Iceland's **oldest surviving man-made dwelling.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Rútshellir

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Hvolsvöllur → Sólheimajökull / Rútshellir

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull / Sólheimajökull
en: Up close the ice isn't white — it's streaked with **black ash bands** from both volcanoes' past tantrums, like a sooty paintbrush dragged across a layered record of the neighbourhood.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull / Sólheimajökull

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull → Reynisfjara / The DC-3 Wreck
en: From the bus you mostly see empty blackness. The real story: a crew that iced up over a glacier, glided to the coast engine-out, and **all seven lived** — on a plane everyone insists on calling by the wrong name.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull → Reynisfjara / The DC-3 Wreck
en: Everyone calls it a "DC-3." It isn't. It's a **US Navy Super DC-3 (a Douglas R4D-8 / C-117D)** — same family, buff cousin who went to the gym. It's worn the wrong name for fifty years.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull → Reynisfjara / The DC-3 Wreck
en: On **21 November 1973** it was flying **Höfn to Keflavík** when **ice choked both carburettors over the Vatnajökull ice cap** and both engines quit. Myth-bust: it did **not** "run out of fuel" — it iced up and became, in the co-pilot's words, "a massively overweight glider."

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull → Reynisfjara / The DC-3 Wreck
en: The pilot turned **south for the coast** and put it down on the black sand. **All seven crew walked away.** The Navy stripped the useful parts and left the bare hull.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Sólheimajökull → Reynisfjara / The DC-3 Wreck
en: For decades a quiet local landmark; then a **Bieber video (2015)** and the Bollywood hit *Dilwale* filmed here, and Instagram did the rest. Cars were banned in **2016**, so now you walk a **4 km track each way** across old ocean floor to touch a plane with no wings. Not a joke in bad weather: the plain has **no shelter at all**, and **two visitors died of hypothermia** near the wreck in a January 2020 storm.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Reynisfjara → Vík / Katla
en: Under that ice sits **Katla** — a **~10 km-wide caldera**, summit **1,512 m** — one of Iceland's biggest, angriest volcanoes. The cap above is **Mýrdalsjökull**, Iceland's **4th-largest ice cap** (~**595 km²**), a **200–700 m** insulating blanket over a furnace. Being subglacial is the whole danger: she doesn't just throw ash, she **flash-melts the glacier into floods.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Reynisfjara → Vík / Katla
en: She's produced **20+ eruptions since 930 CE**, typically **VEI 4–5** — bigger than famous neighbour Eyjafjallajökull's 2010 show. The last major one, **1918**, ran **24 days** and dumped so much flood sediment it **pushed the south coast out about 5 km.** A volcano that does land reclamation.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Reynisfjara → Vík / Katla
en: The rough interval is **every 40–80 years**; the last major was over **100 years ago** — so by any honest reading she's **overdue.** Her system also produced **Eldgjá** around **939 CE**, one of the largest lava floods of the last 2,000 years, and she leaks so much CO₂ while dormant that one study ranked her among **Earth's biggest volcanic CO₂ sources.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Reynisfjara → Vík / Katla
en: Erupting under ice, she makes a **jökulhlaup** — a glacial flood that can push **up to ~300,000 m³ a second** to the sea, faster than a galloping horse. The town ahead, **Vík**, has drilled for this for decades.

en: Iceland's history didn't start with peace. It started with a **slave revolt, a blood feud** — and a vengeful housekeeper who lives in the ice.

ctx: the spoken close — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: Most countries' founding stories are statues and speeches. Iceland's is a body, a fake bear — and a woman who became a volcano.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: **Hjörleifshöfði** — a **221 m móberg headland** — is named for **Hjörleifur Hróðmarsson**, sworn **blood-brother of Ingólfur Arnarson, Iceland's first settler**. The two **sailed here together around 874**, then split: Ingólfur let the gods choose his home, following his high-seat pillars to Reykjavík; Hjörleifur — who **refused to sacrifice to any god** — parked at the first headland. **His burial mound still crowns the summit.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: Come spring, says *Landnámabók*: **one ox** — so his **enslaved Irishmen dragged the plough**. They killed the ox and **blamed a bear**. Iceland **has no bears** — the newcomers just didn't know that yet. When the Norsemen scattered to hunt it, the thralls **ambushed them one by one**, Hjörleifur included, then fled with the women and boats to the islands offshore.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: Ingólfur found the bodies, tracked the killers to those islands, and killed them all. His eulogy: **"A sad end for a good man, slain by slaves — that's what comes of refusing to sacrifice."** Those islands became the **Vestmannaeyjar** — **"Isles of the West Men,"** the Norse name for **Irish Gaels** — **named after the enslaved men who did the deed.**

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: The ghost came **three centuries later**. **Katla**, a fearsome housekeeper at the nearby monastery of **Þykkvabæjarklaustur**, owned **magic breeches that never tired**. Shepherd **Barði** borrowed them; she **drowned him in the whey vat**. When sinking whey threatened to expose the body, she fled onto **Mýrdalsjökull** and **leapt into the chasm still called Kötlugjá — "Katla's rift"** — the volcano's vent. Soon after, a **glacial flood burst from the ice**. **The volcano is named after her** — and every eruption, they say, is her temper.

ctx: fact bullet — tour 5.0 / Vík í Mýrdal / Hjörleifshöfði
en: Like Pétursey, this cape **was once an island** — tethered to Iceland by miles of Katla's black sand.
